title: Closing a Ridgeline Consumer Credit Account — Training Notes
content:
These notes set out the Ridgeline Consumer Credit closure rules as questions a new representative meets.

**Who can close the account, and when?** The primary cardholder may close their account at any time, recorded as an account closure request. Closure takes effect only on the primary cardholder's own confirmation.

**Can an account with a balance be closed?** Where the tier allows closure with a balance owed, yes. The balance is then repaid under the existing terms, promotional plans keep their terms and end dates, and authorized users are removed.

**From which statuses?** An active or a suspended account can be closed on the cardholder's confirmation.

**Can a closed account be reopened?** No. A closed account cannot be reopened; the customer applies again under the holding limits per customer.

**Does the bank ever close an account itself?** Yes, in two cases. It closes a revolving account when the whole calendar months elapsed since the account's last purchase or payment reach the tier's inactivity figure, on a tier where that figure is above 0. It closes a Ridgeline Project Loan whose draw period has ended once its balance reaches 0.00.

**Hypothetical: a revolving card on a 24-month inactivity tier, last purchase or payment 23 whole months ago.** The inactivity figure is not yet reached. At 24 whole months the bank closes it.

**Hypothetical: a Project Loan still in its draw period with a 0.00 balance.** The draw period has not ended, so the payoff closure does not apply.
